newsitem.title: NORWAY: Military exercise for 18 nations in Norway, Sweden.
newsitem.headline: Military exercise for 18 nations in Norway, Sweden.

text.p: Military forces from 18 nations on Monday began the first Partnership for Peace exercise in which land, sea and air forces operate jointly, officials said.

Dubbed "Exercise Co-operative Banners '97", the manoeuvres are being staged in southern Norway and Sweden. About 1,800 ground troops, 37 navy vessels and 45 aircraft are taking part in the exercise, which ends on June 6.

The officials said the naval forces on Monday set out from the port of Gothenburg on the Swedish west coast to sail to the port of Kristiansand on the Norwegian south coast where most of the training will take place.
The air and land forces are already in Norway.

"It is the first so-called joint live exercise in the history of the Partnership for Peace, meaning that it involves land, sea and air forces which operate together with a common mission," a statement by the exercise leaders said.
The exercise, in which eight NATO member states and 10 Partner nations are taking part, is directed by Headquarters Allied Forces North Europe in the Norwegian west coast port of Stavanger.
Western leaders in 1994 adopted the Partnership concept for closer military cooperation with former foes in eastern Europe as well as with neutral nations such as Sweden.
Countries that were once part of the Soviet-led Warsaw Pact are now clamouring to join the 16-nation North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO).
